questions.history: Read slots 1 and 2 via the generated nullable holder readers.
questions.prediction: On little-endian machines the old big-endian interpretation predicts incorrect values. On the merge require the exact positive then negative BigDecimal, both with scale 2. On big-endian hardware the parent may already agree.
questions.basis: The caller supplied the decimal objects before encoding. Vector.getObject is a second public path. A signed unscaled value of −123456789 denotes −1234567.89 at scale 2.
questions.refutation: The merge loses sign or scale, returns the neighboring slot, or disagrees with the original value.

questions.history: Read numeric 0.00 at slot 0 with the holder and vector APIs.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should return BigDecimal with unscaled value 0 and scale 2.
questions.basis: Zero uses an all-zero fixed-width representation, independent of byte order, at byte offset zero.
questions.refutation: A nonzero number, null, or a scale different from 2 on either revision.

questions.history: Store the same negative value in the last slot of DecimalVector and Decimal256Vector, changing only adjacent valid values between two runs. Populate a nullable holder through vector.get, copy its buffer, byte start, precision and scale to the matching non-null holder, and compare nullable and non-null reader outputs.
questions.prediction: On the merge both widths and both kinds of reader should return exactly −1234567.89 in every run regardless of preceding values.
questions.basis: Sign extension changes physical width while preserving the mathematical integer. Slot 2 begins at byte offset 32 or 64 depending on the vector width.
questions.refutation: Changing an adjacent value changes the target, or one width or holder class yields a different result.
